title: Writing for others
description: Write a formal letter, and sign it properly.
grammarNote: A formal letter uses usted, and it opens with Estimado señor or Estimada señora.

explanation.summary: The last level is about register: the same Spanish, said in the way that fits the reader. A letter to a company is not a message to a friend, and Spanish marks the difference clearly.

sections.heading: How a formal letter is built
sections.body: It opens with Estimado señor or Estimada señora, or with the job title: Estimado director. The body uses usted and the third person, and the verbs are formal: le escribo, me permito adjuntar. It closes with an offer, Atentamente, and the name.

examples.es: Estimado señor López: Le escribo para informarle de que su solicitud ha sido aprobada.
examples.en: Dear Mr López: I am writing to inform you that your application has been approved.

examples.es: Me permito adjuntar el informe solicitado.
examples.en: I take the liberty of attaching the requested report.

sections.heading: Formal words, and what to avoid
sections.body: A formal text avoids the contracted al and del, and it says por este motivo instead of por eso. It uses the words for saying that a business uses: solicitar, to request; adjuntar, to attach. And it does not use the word for a thing you have just found out informally, the news in the press.

examples.es: Por este motivo, le solicito una respuesta.
examples.en: For this reason, I request a reply from you.

examples.es: Quedo a la espera de sus comentarios.
examples.en: I look forward to your comments.
